stem: A 24-year-old woman comes to the office due to a persistent facial rash and increased fatigue.  The facial rash worsens after sun exposure, and her fingers "turn blue" in cold weather.  Physical examination shows a facial rash in a butterfly distribution that spares the nasolabial folds.  Laboratory studies reveal several types of autoantibodies directed against components of the cell nucleus.  One of these antibodies targets proteins complexed with small nuclear ribonucleic acid.  These protein-RNA complexes are most likely involved in which of the following cellular functions?​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌

options.text: Aiding mRNA in exiting the nucleus

options.label: B
options.text: Allowing proper functioning of DNA ligase

explanation:
This patient's malar rash, photosensitivity, Raynaud phenomenon ("blue fingers"), and fatigue are consistent with systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease associated with highly specific anti-Smith antibodies.  These antibodies target Smith proteins, which associate with small nuclear RNA (snRNA) to form small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs).

RNA polymerase II transcribes protein-coding genes into pre-mRNA and also synthesizes most spliceosomal snRNAs.  Pre-mRNA undergoes processing to form mature mRNA, including addition of a 5′ methylguanosine cap, addition of a 3′ poly(A) tail, and RNA splicing.  During splicing, snRNPs and additional proteins assemble on pre-mRNA to form the spliceosome, which removes introns and joins the remaining exons.  Mature mRNA is then exported to the cytoplasm, where it serves as a template for protein synthesis.

(Choices A and D)  Poly(A) polymerase adds a poly(A) tail to the 3′ end of an RNA transcript.  The tail helps protect mRNA from degradation and supports nuclear export and efficient translation.  This process does not require spliceosomal snRNPs.

(Choices B and F)  During eukaryotic DNA replication, DNA polymerase delta synthesizes Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand.  After removal of RNA primers and replacement with DNA, DNA ligase seals the remaining nicks to form an intact daughter strand.

(Choice C)  Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases attach amino acids to their corresponding tRNAs, preparing them for translation.  Each synthetase recognizes a specific amino acid and its corresponding tRNAs.

Educational objective:Small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) contain small nuclear RNA and associated proteins.  They are essential components of spliceosomes, which remove introns and join exons during pre-mRNA processing.  Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus can have anti-Smith antibodies directed against protein components of snRNPs.​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌
